topic: sub:12|Relative frequency and probability|Use relative frequency as an estimate of probability

parts.latex: What is the relative frequency of a student eating fast food at least 3 times in one week?

solutions.latex:
At least 3 times means $3$, $4$ or $5$ times, with frequencies $20$, $18$ and $15$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Relative frequency} &= \dfrac{20+18+15}{78} \\ &= \dfrac{53}{78} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
The relative frequency of basketball is $\dfrac{2}{5}$

Use the data in the table to determine the number of students who play basketball on weekends.

A sample of 50 students is to be undertaken to analyse their level of enjoyment in playing their weekend sport.

How many students who play cricket on the weekend, should be included in the sample?

solutions.latex:
The relative frequency of basketball is $\dfrac{2}{5}$, so the other sports make up $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the total, and they total $150$ students.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total students} &= \dfrac{150}{3}\times 5 \\ &= 250 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Basketball} &= 250-150 \\ &= 100 \end{aligned}$$
Therefore 100 students play basketball.
criteria: Finds the total number of students, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. The 150 for other sports is taken from the source working; the table is not shown here.

solutions.latex:
The sample is proportional: 60 of the 250 students play cricket.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cricket in sample} &= \dfrac{60}{250}\times 50 \\ &= 12 \end{aligned}$$
